plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a fixed 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 alternating stack on CaF2 substrate can simultaneously achieve high transmittance in two mid-IR passbands (3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm) while suppressing two stopbands (2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm). This route draws from recalled knowledge of quarter-wave stack design principles adapted for dual-bandpass filters, where high/low index contrast creates stopbands and strategic thickness deviations open transmission windows. The refinement narrows thickness bounds around the best-performing candidate from the prior round to exploit the promising region already identified.

routes.title: Refined 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 dual-bandpass filter with localized thickness optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 22-layer alternating ZnS/Al2O3 stack with thicknesses tuned around the empirically successful region from round 1 will improve the tightest_margin while maintaining or improving the best_target_score, demonstrating that local refinement outperforms broad exploration for this topology.
routes.design_principle: Recalled knowledge of dielectric multilayer filters suggests that once a promising thickness configuration is found, local coordinate descent with reduced step size can refine the solution toward better robustness without escaping the basin of attraction. The high index contrast between ZnS (n~2.4 in mid-IR) and Al2O3 (n~1.6 in mid-IR) provides sufficient optical contrast for stopband formation.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | Daimon-20 substrate (22 coating layers total)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers, bounded to ±30 nm around the median thickness values from the best-performing candidate in round 1
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.20-4.30 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.45-5.00 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 22 (within 24-layer limit)
ZnS and Al2O3 are conventional IR-depositable dielectrics
Thickness bounds restricted to narrow range for manufacturability consistency
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: High/low index alternating stacks create photonic stopbands centered at quarter-wave optical thickness
Recalled knowledge: Dual passbands can be opened by introducing controlled thickness deviations from quarter-wave condition at strategic layer positions
Recalled knowledge: Local refinement with reduced step size typically improves robustness metrics once a promising region is identified
Recalled knowledge: ZnS has higher refractive index than Al2O3 in the mid-IR, providing index contrast for interference effects
Recalled knowledge: CaF2 (Daimon-20 dataset) is transparent in the 2.5-5.0 μm range and serves as suitable IR substrate
expected_advantages: Narrower bounds reduce search space and focus computation on promising region
Smaller optimizer step size allows finer tuning of thickness values
Maintaining the same material pair isolates thickness optimization as the only variable
Building on round 1's best candidate leverages already-discovered successful configuration
known_risks: Uncertainty about exact n/k values for ZnS and Al2O3 at 3-5 μm wavelengths; recalled values are approximate
Uncertainty whether ±30 nm bounds are too restrictive -- may prevent escape from local optimum if the round 1 best is not near global optimum
Recalled knowledge suggests quarter-wave thickness near 1250 nm for 3-5 μm band, but actual optimal thicknesses may differ significantly
No literature verification of ZnS/Al2O3 compatibility or stress issues in 22-layer stacks
Daimon-20 dataset selection was made to resolve registry ambiguity; other CaF2 datasets (Daimon-25) may have slightly different optical properties
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer thin-film stack on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat) (22 coating layers). Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses with bounds set to ±30 nm around these center values: [962, 612, 734, 659, 459, 1168, 384, 593, 862, 479, 484, 1139, 337, 437, 852, 446, 824, 1233, 945, 389, 816, 870] nm. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with reduced learning rate for local refinement. Evaluate transmittance at four wavelength bands: 2500-3100 nm (suppress), 3250-3350 nm (pass), 4200-4300 nm (pass), 4450-5000 nm (suppress). No metal layers. Coherent TMM calculation under frequency-domain plane-wave illumination.
routes.revision_reason: Round 2 refinement: Narrow thickness bounds to ±30 nm around round 1 best candidate medians, reduce optimizer step size for local coordinate descent to improve tightest_margin from 0.393. Repaired substrate name from CaF2 to Daimon-20 to resolve registry ambiguity.

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route fails to produce physically valid candidates after bound relaxation, the topology or material pair may be fundamentally unsuitable for this dual-bandpass requirement and would need literature-guided redesign.

tightest_margin should increase above 0.393386 as local refinement improves robustness
valid_candidates count should remain similar or increase as bounds are more constrained around feasible region
thicknesses_nm should cluster tightly around the round 1 best candidate values with small variations
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if tightest_margin fails to improve over three consecutive rounds despite thickness refinement, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops below 5, relax thickness bounds to ±50 nm and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
